items.title: This is Software's iPhone Moment
items.summary: The iPhone didn't end professional photography. It made taking pictures an everyday reflex: we went from 85 billion photos a year to 2.1 trillion. But the value didn't go to the people taking the pictures. It went to whoever owned the platform.AI is doing the same thing to software. As a billion new creators come online, most of what they build will be personal, disposable, and look a lot like a hackathon project. Their agents will pick the stack, and nearly all of it is built on open source maintained by a small group of people.This talk covers what software's iPhone moment means for developers, maintainers, companies, platforms, and everyone else, and why open source and open intelligence are our chance to make sure the tools belong to everyone this time.Find or host a Hacktoberfest event near you: hacktoberfest.comThis talk was delivered at All Things Open 2026 in Raleigh, NC, USA
